correctness.rationale: The kernel identity holds pointwise off the diagonal for every integer m and every complex parameter. Independent moments give exact rank m; noncritical finite-rank perturbation of injective J^m gives infinite rank. A periodic Fourier inverse of the mth derivative differs from J^m by a polynomial-range operator (rank at most m+1), yielding exact s_n asymptotic via rank perturbation interlacing and the p-series threshold. The full-rank anti-diagonal moment matrix proves normality and exact inertia; a Hilbert Cauchy determinant yields positive eigenvalue product. Exact symbolic checks of the critical identities passed 159 cases for m<=12 and monomials (m<=8). Limitations: checks are finite; proof is universal.

value.rationale: For the canonical opposing-direction smoothing pencil, the result gives a complete all-order classification of the precise parameter where infinite rank drops to m, the otherwise sharp asymptotic scale and operator-ideal threshold, and the parity-dependent full signed spectral counts and exact eigenvalue product. This is a natural intrinsic structural question, not an arbitrary slice; the finite-rank limit creates the precise effective-dimensional and normality boundary. Individual polynomial identities and known low-order cases are acknowledged as ingredients, not the claimed standalone value.
